summary: I independently reviewed H1 E3301's frozen probe, stdout, execution record, source pins, and receipt against the pinned source. The captured actual volatile-fixture flow supports the reuse conclusion for the deletion-recovery hypothesis: a rendered own-topic delete succeeds, stale detail renders the unavailable fallback and Back to Forum, returning preserves the search and exposes the no-results state, and Clear search restores the three seeded topics without additional runtime receipts. The earlier source-level gap candidate is falsified as an unreachable recovery problem; do not force a patch.

sourceReview.sourcePins: All seven hashes in H1 source-pins.json match current source: community.mjs, public-controller.mjs, public-site.mjs, runtime.mjs, fixture-provider.mjs, teacher-journey.mjs, public-controller.test.mjs.

assertionReview: Assertions directly prove: fixture initializes; after-initialize receipt count is 2; teacher role control, topic form, matching index result card, and rendered delete action are present; created topic belongs to demo-teacher; rendered event payload carries matching postId/threadId; store delete succeeds and getThread returns null; deleted detail exposes a Back to Forum link; return renders an empty-state node; Clear search restores three seeded topic cards; deleted ID is absent and receipt count remains 2.

Captured (not separately asserted) observations include the exact stale detail route, unavailable-detail text, zero topic-card count on return, retained query, and status messages; these agree with the pinned controller/renderer behavior.

The route behavior is manual recovery, not automatic redirect: successful forum-delete-post refreshes community state but leaves /posts/:id in place. The actual rendered back link and index recovery make this bounded recovery path reachable, so the proposed defect was not demonstrated.

The execution does not test anonymous/foreign-owner rejection, moderator behavior, hidden-topic deletion, stale payloads, or reply deletion. Source-level authorization review remains useful but is not executed guard proof; do not generalize this probe into acceptance of those controls or reply lifecycle.
Volatile storage is null, so evidence is in-memory fixture behavior only; no persisted-session recovery claim is supported.
